title: Multidimensional Linear Cryptanalysis for QFT Key Recovery
summary: Independent multiple-linear statistics reduce variance in QFT-based key recovery; whether multidimensional linear cryptanalysis can replace them, with a corresponding analysis, remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the QFT-based key-recovery framework, multiple linear approximations are analyzed using statistically independent relations, whose statistics have smaller variance and therefore make distinguishing the correct key easier. Multidimensional linear cryptanalysis instead uses a set of linear approximations whose masks form a linear subspace, making the statistical analysis more robust to dependencies, but its use in this framework has not been analyzed. Determine whether multidimensional linear cryptanalysis can replace the independent multiple-linear statistic in this QFT-based framework, and derive the corresponding statistical analysis.

scope.domain: Quantum symmetric-key cryptanalysis using QFT-based linear key recovery and multidimensional linear cryptanalysis.
assumptions: The existing multiple-linear analysis uses statistically independent relations.
parameters: Set of linear approximations — its masks form the linear subspace used in multidimensional linear cryptanalysis
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether multidimensional linear cryptanalysis can replace the independent multiple-linear statistic in the QFT-based framework and derive the resulting statistical analysis.

citations.label: Quantum Linear Key-recovery Attacks Using the QFT

progress.summary: The source shows that multiple linear approximations reduce variance and aid QFT-based attacks. It presents multidimensional linear cryptanalysis as an untried but plausible replacement that may handle dependencies more robustly.
citation_labels: André Schrottenloher et al., Quantum Linear Key-recovery Attacks Using the QFT
